news.title: AI refutes 30-year-old mathematical assumption in computer science
paras: “This came as a complete surprise, a shock,” says Fedor Fomin at the University of Bergen in Norway. Proposed nearly 30 years ago, the exponential time hypothesis (ETH) tries to put a limit on how quickly computers can solve certain logical puzzles.

The simplest way would be to try every possible combination of true or false for each part of the puzzle. ETH proposes that, although it may be possible to do this quicker with shortcuts, the amount of work needed has to grow exponentially as the puzzle gets bigger.

news.title: Clean-up underway as tens of thousands of homes left without power after Storm Boelo
paras: Storm Boelo battered parts of the north of England, Northern Ireland and Scotland this weekend, and as of 7pm on Sunday night, 90,000 homes were still without power according to the Energy Network Agency. Winds of 85mph were recorded on Saturday, and the high winds caused lots of damage in affected areas.

Published 1 September Boelo came soon after Storm Austen brought strong winds and heavy rain on Friday, leaving many homes in the South West of England without power. An amber warning for wind was in place for Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and parts of northern England on Saturday and Sunday.

news.title: Brazil election: President Lula da Silva beats Flavio Bolsonaro
paras: It is home to the Amazon rainforest - the so-called 'lungs of the world', because of the role it plays in absorbing carbon dioxide and producing oxygen . And on Sunday night, left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated right-wing rival Flávio Bolsonaro in a closely fought election.

80-year-old President Lula da Silva won the election in a surprise victory, with just over half of the vote - 51.79%. He had been trailing behind Mr Bolsonaro after the first round of voting. Published 4 days ago Official count data suggests there were around four million votes between the two candidates.

news.title: 'I didn't know our great-grandma did such amazing things'
paras: Well, Press Packers Elise and Renae's great-grandmother Locita Brandy has won a Manchester University Medal of Honour. She was one of the founders of the Manchester Caribbean Carnival and also fought against racism in education.

The award is for her community work and for many years campaigning to help black children. The sisters went to interview Locita for Newsround to find out more about her life and how she improved things for many black children. They discovered some of her achievements, like changing school dinners, leading Saturday school so kids from the Caribbean could learn about their heritage, and getting books with racist language removed from the school library.

news.title: US and Israel launch attacks on Iran
paras: The US and Israel have launched attacks on Iran, which is a country in the Middle East. US President Donald Trump said in a video that the American military has begun "major combat operations" in Iran.

In a statement, Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that his country was working with the US to remove what he called a threat to both countries. It comes after US talks with Iran to try and stop them from developing a nuclear weapon, something that Iran denies it is doing. news.title: Tanzania celebrates first natural gas discovery in more than 10 years
paras: Tanzania has announced a significant discovery of natural gas in the Mnazi Bay area in the south of the country - the first such find in a decade.

Energy Minister Juma Homera attended a ceremony at the Kasa-1X ST2 well, which is jointly owned by state-owned Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation (TPDC) and French oil firm Maurel & Prom, to mark the occasion. He said the estimated 223 billion cubic feet (6.3 billion cubic metres) discovery was a "major milestone" in the development of the small oil and gas sector in the East African nation.

news.title: A bust-up between mathematicians is fuelling fears that AI could undermine science
paras: A bust-up between mathematicians is fuelling fears that AI could undermine science Inside: dozens of small boxes with barcoded glass tubes, collectively containing one hundred billion genes. Just two boxes may hold 10 times more information than all the text on the internet, says Dr Oliver Vince, the facility's co-founder.

Vince, like many in business and academic research, believes AI will supercharge scientific research. But increasingly, it also comes with controversy. Last month, OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, said it had solved one of maths' great unsolved problems, relating to the famous Navier–Stokes equations.

news.title: Girl seriously injured in wolf attack at German wildlife park
paras: An eight-year-old girl has been seriously injured in a wolf attack at a German wildlife park. She was inside an enclosure at the Johannismühle park in Brandenburg, south of Berlin, with a staff member and two other children when the attack happened, police said.

They said in a statement that the "precise circumstances of the incident are the subject of an ongoing police investigation". The girl was taken to hospital by helicopter after the incident on Wednesday. The park, in the town of Baruth/Mark, has been closed temporarily and is set to reopen on 2 November, according to its website, which did not give further details.

news.title: Bloodied, dazed and angry - how passengers' rail journey turned to disaster in Spain
paras: It was approaching 08:30 (07:30 GMT) on a normal Wednesday. Two high-speed trains were travelling south from the Spanish capital, Madrid, to Seville. One, run by state-owned operator Renfe had 397 passengers on board.

Ahead of it on the same line was a train of Iryo private operator with 147 passengers. A reported issue with the automatic signalling system - a computer failure - had forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch. Then the impossible happened, Spain's transport minister said, as the Renfe train was ordered to proceed in "error".

news.title: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
paras: Partial results from Israel's general election show veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is leading his rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, but is still short of a majority in parliament. With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies were on track to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.

Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc were set for 48. Arab-led parties, who are on course to win an unprecedented 19 seats, could emerge as kingmakers, but all but one of the Jewish parties have pledged not to work with them.

news.title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction
paras: The mounted skeleton of a newly-identified dinosaur once mistaken for a young Tyrannosaurus rex has sold at auction for a colossal $47.3m (£35.5m). Nicknamed Jodi, the roughly 10-foot-tall (3m) skeleton was auctioned by Sotheby's in New York. The sale comes a year after researchers confirmed that the skeleton belongs to a distinct genus.

The Late Cretaceous carnivore was expected to fetch at least $9m when it went under the hammer on Tuesday. The auction comes after Sotheby's sold a Tyrannosaurus rex, dubbed Gus, for a record $50.1m in July. The sale has reignited debate in the scientific community over whether dinosaur remains should be sold privately or displayed publicly.

news.title: Is Taekwondo an art or A Sport?
paras: And then… silence, and then someone from the crowd shouted… “Is Taekwondo a sport or is it a performing arts?” Well we are here to answer that question! Did you know that Taekwondo is Korean? In Korean, chung and hung mean blue and red.
